executive_summary: The q128 numeric matcher is exact for all 3000 independently reconstructed transactions, including lowest-ID selection, signed residual masks, fallback selection, ordering, backpressure stability and latency. However, M348 is not contract-complete: after a protocol error, a legal eight-beat configuration can resurrect cfg_active without reset while cfg_protocol_error remains asserted. This violates the stated fail-closed-until-reset contract and the shipped SVA. The shipped test immediately resets after its only attack and therefore misses the bug. M348 closes the isolated center/ID/signed-mask datapath portion of M335-P0-02, but it does not yet connect the frozen q128 catalog, PWP addressing or M307 trace conservation, so M335-P0-02 remains open at the executable interface level. M335-P0-01 is unrelated and unchanged.

independent_trace_reconstruction.method: Fresh exact-source VCS build with read-only top-level signal trace; an independent standard-library parser reconstructed accepted inputs and retired outputs and recomputed the 128-center reference without using the shipped scoreboard.

sequence: accept invalid configuration group 1 before group 0
without reset, accept legal groups 0 through 7 with commit only on group 7
protocol_counterexample.contract_violation: The contract says any ordering or commit error fails closed until reset. cfg_active may not reassert while sticky cfg_protocol_error remains high.
protocol_counterexample.root_cause: cfg_ready is only gated by pipeline emptiness, and the configuration state machine continues accepting beats after cfg_protocol_error. The legal group-7 path sets cfg_active without clearing or guarding the sticky error.
protocol_counterexample.existing_tb_blind_spot: The shipped test performs one out-of-order attack and immediately resets, so it never tries configuration traffic while cfg_protocol_error is sticky.
minimum_fix: Gate cfg_ready and configuration-state updates with !cfg_protocol_error.
Add a no-reset legal-reconfiguration attempt after every protocol attack and require cfg_active=0, cfg_ready=0 and in_ready=0 until reset.
Rerun exact-SHA VCS and retain the sticky-error SVA as an asserted invariant.

architecture_checks.lowest_id_tie_break: PASS: stage 0 initializes ID 0 and later stages replace only on strict lower distance; independent 3000-transaction recomputation found zero winner mismatches.
architecture_checks.global_stall: PASS_AT_OBSERVED_INTERFACE: every pipeline register advances only under global advance=!out_valid||out_ready; output payload was stable on 609 stalled cycles.
architecture_checks.ii1: PASS_DIRECTED: maximum consecutive input accepts=513 and consecutive output retires=407.
architecture_checks.latency: PASS_DIRECTED: no-stall minimum is exactly 128 cycles; backpressure extends observed latency to 178.
architecture_checks.configuration: FAIL_FAIL_CLOSED; nominal eight-beat sequence passes, but sticky-error recovery is invalid.
architecture_checks.pattern_reload: STRUCTURALLY_PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNVERIFIED: configuration waits for an empty pipeline and cfg_valid blocks inputs, but no shipped reload-under-traffic/drain regression proves atomic catalog replacement.
architecture_checks.reset: UNDERTESTED: reset is tested before workload and immediately after one attack, not mid-configuration or mid-pipeline.
architecture_checks.synthesis_feasibility: UNCHARACTERIZED: 127 parallel 16-bit XOR/popcount comparisons, roughly 6.4 kbit of pipeline state, 2 kbit of pattern flops, a high-fanout global advance, a 128-way nonempty reduction and pervasive asynchronous reset require DC/Fmax/area characterization and equal-area comparison.

M335-P0-01.reason: The FC2 4.764209x denominator namespace error is unrelated to this matcher. M348 does not authorize transferring that ratio to Conv.

M335-P0-02.repaired: M348 emits unconditional nearest center, lowest center ID, distance, population, original pattern and signed residual masks for a synthetic q128 catalog.
M335-P0-02.still_missing: No RTL-connected frozen q128 catalog/PWP memory interface, PWP address issue, tau1011 selected-assignment conservation miter, finite queues or M307 ordered-trace replay exists. Therefore the executable Conv interface is not closed.

findings.title: Sticky configuration error does not keep cfg_active fail-closed until reset
findings.evidence: Fresh VCS counterexample reaches cfg_protocol_error=1,cfg_active=1,in_ready=0 by issuing a legal eight-beat configuration after an invalid beat without reset.
findings.impact: The RTL violates its explicit configuration contract and shipped SVA; external control can observe an active catalog in an error state.
findings.required_fix: Reject all configuration handshakes and state updates while cfg_protocol_error is asserted; add sticky-error follow-on attacks to TB/SVA.

findings.title: M348 repairs only the isolated numeric half of M335-P0-02
findings.evidence: The directed catalog and synthetic transactions prove center/ID/mask semantics, but there is no frozen M307 assignment trace, PWP address/memory, tau1011 conservation or finite executor connection.
findings.impact: M348 cannot yet be used to admit complete PWP Conv cycles or claim that M335-P0-02 is closed.
findings.required_fix: Connect the exact matcher to frozen catalog/PWP identity and replay selected assignment rows through an address-bearing, finite ready/valid interface.

findings.title: The receipt tie metric counts transient-best equality, not final nearest ties
findings.evidence: The shipped scoreboard increments on equality with the best distance at that point in the scan. Independent recomputation finds 1211 transactions with a final nearest tie and 2729 extra final-nearest centers, versus the reported 12730 transient equality observations.
findings.impact: The coverage gate remains nonzero and lowest-ID behavior is correct, but the receipt label overstates the number of nearest-tie observations.
findings.required_fix: Rename the existing count or compute ties only after the final minimum distance is known.

findings.title: Protocol, reload, reset and internal pipeline assertions are incomplete
findings.evidence: No test covers early or missing final commit, duplicate/group skip matrix, sticky-error traffic, reset mid-config/mid-pipeline, catalog reload while draining, internal 128-stage stall stability, exact latency or center-ID-to-pattern consistency.
findings.impact: The numeric scoreboard is strong, but control corner cases can escape—as demonstrated by M350-P1-01.
findings.required_fix: Add a configuration protocol matrix, reset/reload/backpressure sequences and structural assertions for stage freeze, order, latency and selected center identity.

findings.title: The 128-stage implementation has no synthesis or equal-area evidence
findings.evidence: M348 has no DC/Fmax/area result and stores the catalog in flops while replicating 127 popcount/compare stages under a global stall net.
findings.impact: II1 functionality cannot yet be compared fairly with SERIAL16 or used for throughput/mm2, energy or paper PPA claims.
findings.required_fix: After protocol repair, run exact-SHA DC and compare area/Fmax/throughput against an equal-area SERIAL16 baseline before Formality/PTPX.

coverage_blind_spots: configuration after sticky protocol error without reset
early commit, missing final commit, duplicate group, skipped group and post-error cfg_valid persistence
catalog reload after prior active use and while the pipeline is draining
reset during partial configuration, full pipeline and output stall
internal per-stage payload stability under global stall
asserted exact 128-cycle no-stall latency and transaction order
final-nearest tie coverage distinct from transient scan equality

dc.reason: Characterizing a known contract-invalid RTL would not create an admissible PPA point. First fix fail-closed control and rerun exact-SHA VCS; then exploratory logic-only DC is appropriate.

formality.reason: Requires corrected RTL, clean DC netlist, pinned reference and explicit compare constraints.

ptpx.reason: Requires repaired and synthesized RTL, formal equivalence, representative SAIF including backpressure/catalog behavior, and explicit memory macro or memory-energy accounting.

ordered_next_actions: Repair sticky-error fail-closed behavior and extend TB/SVA with no-reset reconfiguration, protocol matrix, reset and reload attacks.
Rerun exact-SHA VCS and repeat the independent 3000-transaction/reference trace audit.
Run exploratory DC/Fmax/area and equal-area SERIAL16 normalization on the repaired SHA.
Connect center ID to frozen catalog/PWP addressing and prove tau1011 selected-assignment conservation on the frozen M307 trace.
Only then proceed to Formality, representative SAIF/PTPX and cycle claims.
